$comment: Idiom of the week. Each idiom and its meaning is checked against SSČ/SSJČ as shown in the Internetová jazyková příručka (ÚJČ AV ČR); the example sentences are new and need native review.

idioms.literal: to have butter on your head
idioms.meaning: to have done something wrong yourself, so you are in no position to criticise or act freely
idioms.definitionCs: lze ho postihnout pro minulé provinění

example.cs: Neříkej mu nic o pozdních příchodech, sám má máslo na hlavě.
example.en: Don't lecture him about being late: he's got butter on his head himself.

idioms.label: expr.

idioms.literal: to walk around hot porridge
idioms.meaning: to avoid a subject or decision
idioms.definitionCs: vyhýbat se řešení něčeho, mluvení o něčem

example.cs: Nechoď kolem horké kaše a řekni mi to.
example.en: Stop walking around the hot porridge and tell me.

idioms.label: expr.

idioms.cs: jako když hrách na stěnu hází
idioms.literal: like throwing peas at a wall
idioms.meaning: pointless: talking to someone who will not listen

example.cs: Domlouvat mu je jako hrách na stěnu házet.
example.en: Reasoning with him is like throwing peas at a wall.

idioms.english: like talking to a brick wall

idioms.literal: to carry wood into the forest
idioms.meaning: to do something pointless, bringing what is already there

example.cs: Nosit do Prahy pivo je jako nosit dříví do lesa.
example.en: Bringing beer to Prague is carrying wood into the forest.

idioms.literal: to buy a hare in a sack
idioms.meaning: to buy something without seeing or testing it

example.cs: Byt bez prohlídky? To je kupovat zajíce v pytli.
example.en: A flat without a viewing? That's buying a hare in a sack.

idioms.english: to buy a pig in a poke

idioms.literal: that is where the dog is buried
idioms.meaning: that is the real problem, the catch

example.cs: Nájem je levný, ale nikdo tam nechce bydlet. Kde je zakopaný pes?
example.en: The rent is cheap but nobody wants to live there. Where's the dog buried?

idioms.literal: to drink yourself under the picture
idioms.meaning: to get completely drunk

example.cs: Na firemním večírku se zpil pod obraz.
example.en: He drank himself under the picture at the office party.

idioms.label: expr.

idioms.literal: to carry owls to Athens
idioms.meaning: to teach someone something they know better than you, which is pointless
idioms.definitionCs: poučovat někoho, kdo ví něco lépe, a tím dělat něco zbytečného

example.cs: Vysvětlovat Čechovi, jak se točí pivo? To je nosit sovy do Athén.
example.en: Explaining to a Czech how to pour beer? That's carrying owls to Athens.

idioms.english: to teach your grandmother to suck eggs

idioms.literal: to make a camel out of a mosquito
idioms.meaning: to blow something up out of all proportion

example.cs: Jedna chyba v e-mailu, nedělej z komára velblouda.
example.en: One typo in an email: don't make a camel out of a mosquito.

idioms.english: to make a mountain out of a molehill
idioms.label: expr.

idioms.literal: dark as in a sack
idioms.meaning: pitch dark

example.cs: V listopadu je v pět večer tma jako v pytli.
example.en: In November it's dark as in a sack by five.

idioms.label: expr.

idioms.literal: it goes as if on butter
idioms.meaning: it goes smoothly, without problems

example.cs: Na úřadě to dnes šlo jako po másle.
example.en: At the office today it all went as if on butter.

idioms.literal: to throw your rifle into the rye
idioms.meaning: to give up, lose heart (usually after a first setback)
idioms.definitionCs: ztratit, ztrácet odvahu pokračovat (po neúspěchu), vzdát se

example.cs: Čeština je těžká, ale flintu do žita neházej.
example.en: Czech is hard, but don't throw your rifle into the rye.

idioms.label: hovor.

idioms.literal: to have it done for fear
idioms.meaning: to be fearless

example.cs: Jezdí na kole po Václaváku, ten má pro strach uděláno.
example.en: He cycles down Wenceslas Square: nothing scares him.

idioms.literal: to sit on two chairs
idioms.meaning: to play both sides, be two-faced

example.cs: Nemůžeš pracovat pro obě firmy, nesedí se na dvou židlích.
example.en: You can't work for both companies: you can't sit on two chairs.

idioms.english: to have a foot in both camps

idioms.literal: to climb into someone's cabbage
idioms.meaning: to meddle in someone else's business (also: to go after their partner)
idioms.definitionCs: zasahovat do jeho působnosti; přebírat mu dívku

example.cs: Tohle je můj projekt, nelez mi do zelí.
example.en: This is my project: stay out of my cabbage.

idioms.cs: to je pro mě španělská vesnice
idioms.literal: that is a Spanish village to me
idioms.meaning: I don't understand it at all

example.cs: Daňové přiznání je pro mě španělská vesnice.
example.en: My tax return is a Spanish village to me.

idioms.literal: the apple doesn't fall far from the tree
idioms.meaning: children turn out like their parents

example.cs: Její táta je taky kuchař. Jablko nepadá daleko od stromu.
example.en: Her dad is a chef too. The apple doesn't fall far from the tree.

idioms.english: the apple doesn't fall far from the tree
idioms.label: pořek.

idioms.literal: to talk into the wind
idioms.meaning: to talk in vain; to make empty promises

example.cs: Pronajímatel slíbil opravu, ale mluvil do větru.
example.en: The landlord promised a repair, but he was talking into the wind.

idioms.literal: it is clearer than the sun
idioms.meaning: it is completely obvious

example.cs: Že prší, když zapomenu deštník, je nad slunce jasnější.
example.en: That it rains when I forget my umbrella is clearer than the sun.

idioms.cs: vidět si jen na špičku nosu
idioms.literal: to see only to the tip of your nose
idioms.meaning: to be short-sighted, see only your own interests

example.cs: Plánuje jen do pátku, vidí si jen na špičku nosu.
example.en: He plans only until Friday: he sees only to the tip of his nose.

idioms.english: can't see beyond the end of your nose
idioms.label: hovor. expr.

idioms.literal: to take the wind out of someone's sails
idioms.meaning: to get ahead of someone and spoil their plans
idioms.definitionCs: předejít ho v něčem, zhatit mu plány

example.cs: Kolega řekl můj nápad na poradě dřív a vzal mi vítr z plachet.
example.en: A colleague said my idea at the meeting first and took the wind out of my sails.

idioms.english: to take the wind out of someone's sails
